Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.

# Green Party Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Overview
The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and public service challenges. It proposes significant public investment funded through wealth taxation, carbon taxes, and borrowing.

## Healthcare
The party proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030 and £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, providing universal NHS dentistry (£3bn annually by 2030), improving staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. Mental health services would receive investment to ensure 28-day access to therapies.

## Social Care
Proposals include £20bn annual investment, free personal care modelled on Scotland's system, improved pay and career structures for care workers, and enhanced support for disabled people including a 5% uplift in disability benefits.

## Housing
The manifesto proposes building 150,000 social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering local authorities to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and investing £29bn over five years in home insulation. Planning reforms would prioritise community needs and environmental protection.

## Energy
Plans include achieving 70% wind-powered electricity by 2030, ending new fossil fuel licences and subsidies, introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne, community ownership of energy infrastructure, and opposing new nuclear development. Water companies would return to public ownership.

## Economy and Taxation
The party proposes £40bn average annual green investment, nationalisation of railways and water companies, a wealth tax on assets above £10m, capital gains tax alignment with income tax rates, and a £15 minimum wage. Support for small businesses would include regional mutual banks and grants for decarbonisation.

## Workers' Rights
Commitments include repealing anti-union legislation, implementing maximum 10:1 pay ratios, equal rights for gig economy workers, and moving toward a four-day working week.

## Welfare
Proposals include £40 weekly Universal Credit increase, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, ending the five-week benefit wait, increasing carer's allowance by 10%, and working toward Universal Basic Income.

## Environment
The manifesto proposes a Rights of Nature Act giving legal personhood to nature, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, £3bn annual grants for nature restoration, strengthening pesticide regulations, and introducing right to roam legislation.

## Education
Plans include £8bn school investment, £2bn teacher pay uplift, £5bn for special needs provision, free school meals for all children, abolishing tuition fees, and restoring maintenance grants.

## Transport
Proposals include £10bn annual public transport subsidies, free bus travel for under-18s, bringing railways into public ownership, £2.5bn annual cycling infrastructure investment, ending petrol/diesel vehicle sales by 2027, and a frequent-flyer levy.

## Democracy and Rights
The party proposes proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, repealing voter ID requirements, defending the Human Rights Act, and supporting devolution.

## Immigration
Commitments include ending the hostile environment policy, creating safe asylum routes, ending minimum income requirements for spousal visas, and allowing asylum seekers to work.

## Foreign Policy
The manifesto supports an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian state recognition, ending UK arms sales to Israel, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI, rejoining the EU, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident.

## Funding
Revenue would come from personal wealth and income taxes (estimated £50-70bn annually), business taxes (£40bn over five years), and carbon taxes (up to £80bn annually by parliament's end). Additional borrowing would fund capital investment, with spending increasing from approximately £122bn in year one to £252bn by year five.
